Let \(C=(0,0)\), \(A=(450,0)\), and \(B=(300\cos\theta,300\sin\theta)\). Then \(K=(225,0)\).

By the Angle Bisector Theorem,
\[
\frac{AL}{LB}=\frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{450}{300}=\frac32.
\]
Thus
\[
L=\frac{2A+3B}{5}=(180(1+\cos\theta),180\sin\theta).
\]
So line \(CL\) has direction \((1+\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\).

Let \(P\) be on \(CL\):
\[
P=s(1+\cos\theta,\sin\theta).
\]
Since \(P\) also lies on \(BK\), write
\[
P=K+\lambda(B-K).
\]
Solving gives \(\lambda=\frac37\), so
\[
P=\frac{900}{7}(1+\cos\theta,\sin\theta).
\]

Since \(K\) is the midpoint of \(PM\),
\[
M=2K-P.
\]
Thus
\[
AM=\left|M-A\right|
=\frac{900}{7}\sqrt{(1+\cos\theta)^2+\sin^2\theta}
=\frac{1800}{7}\cos\frac\theta2.
\]
Given \(AM=180\),
\[
\frac{1800}{7}\cos\frac\theta2=180
\implies \cos\frac\theta2=\frac7{10}.
\]

Finally,
\[
LP=\left(180-\frac{900}{7}\right)\sqrt{(1+\cos\theta)^2+\sin^2\theta}
=\frac{360}{7}\cdot 2\cos\frac\theta2
=\frac{720}{7}\cdot \frac7{10}=72.
\]

\[
\boxed{72}
\]
